'''Panada''' or '''''panado''''' is a variety of [[bread soup]] found in some [[Western Europe]]an and [[Southern Europe|Southern European]] cuisines and consisting of [[Staling|stale bread]] boiled to a pulp in water or other liquids.

A version of panada was a favorite dish of the author [[Percy Bysshe Shelley]], who was a vegetarian, covered in sugar and raisins.<ref>Hogg, Thomas Jefferson. ''The Life of Percy Bysshe Shelley''.G Routledge & Sons, 1906</ref> It was considered a light dish suitable for invalids or [[postpartum confinement|women who had just given birth]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Buchan|first1=William|title=Domestic Medicine: A Treatise on the Prevention and Cure of Diseases, by Regimen and Simple Medicines|date=1838|page=587}}</ref>

In [[French cuisine]], it is often enriched with butter, milk, cream, or egg yolk.<ref>[http://atilf.atilf.fr/dendien/scripts/tlfiv5/visusel.exe?12;s=2941315605;r=1;nat=;sol=1; ''Trésor de la langue française'', ''s.v.'' 'panade']</ref>

In [[northeast Italy]], it serves as an inexpensive meal in the poor areas of the countryside. It may be enriched with [[Eggs as food|eggs]], beef [[broth]], and grated cheese. Traditionally, it was frequently prepared as a meal for elderly or ill people.

In [[Spanish cuisine]], it is made by boiling bread in water or milk and adding flavoring.
